title: Prototype catalogue & onboarding pocket notes
summary: Pocket notes for a lightweight Prototype Catalogue: a browsable collection of runnable starter projects (templates + minimal infra + example prompts) to speed up developer onboarding, customer proofs-of-concept, and internal feature demos.
background: We repeatedly see engineers (both new hires and customers) spinning up tiny prototypes to validate model choices, routing policies, and UI integrations. Each prototype reimplements wiring (auth, model selection, prompt plumbing, billing/usage toggles). Idea: keep canonical, curated starter kits in one place (catalog + CLI + brief runbook) so people can clone+run quickly and files stay in sync with our model/runtime changes.
goals: Reduce time-to-first-prototype from days -> minutes for internal engineers and early customers
Provide curated templates that are explicitly compatible with hosted / dedicated / private modes
Make prototypes discoverable and runnable with a single CLI command or one-click deploy
Ensure catalogue templates include security/runbook notes and minimal telemetry opt-in
user_stories: As a new backend engineer, I want a simple template that wires Redwood API calls, so I can test response shapes without building infra
As a solutions engineer, I want a repo with a demo app + sample prompts for a chosen model so I can spin up a customer POC during a call
As a platform engineer, I want to know which templates are compatible with Private (VPC/on-prem) so I can provide accurate guidance
As a product PM, I want to flag templates with maturity + last-tested date so we don't ship stale examples
acceptance_criteria: Catalog exists as a small Git repo + metadata index (YAML/JSON) listing templates
CLI: `rwd proto init <template>` clones + installs deps + prints run steps; successful run launches demo server in <3 commands
Each template has: README with purpose, model compatibility tags (hosted/dedicated/private), minimal security notes, link to runbook
At least 4 templates initially: quick-text-gen (hosted), chat-with-history (dedicated), private-onprem-sample, embedding-search-demo
Template tests: CI smoke test that runs a single inference call against a test token (mock or staging) and exits 0
Telemetry opt-in prompt implemented in CLI, and telemetry events defined (proto:init, proto:run, proto:error)
open_questions: Permission model: where do templates live (public repo vs internal monorepo)? Who can add/approve templates?
Secrets/credentials: provide sample env vars vs integrated secrets manager? How to avoid accidental creds leak
Versioning: how to keep templates in sync with model catalog changes (e.g., deprecations / quantized variants)?
Private compatibility: do we include example manifests for private installers or separate minimal config snippets?
Billing implications: do we surface cost estimates for running a template (tokens / GPU hours)? If yes, who pays for demo runs in sales calls?

Schedule 30-min sync with Mira + Ravi to review phasing and ownership
rough_mocks: Catalog UI - left rail: categories (quickstarts, customer-pocs, infra-examples); center: cards with 1-line purpose + labels (hosted/dedicated/private) + last-tested badge
Template card detail: demo gif, 3-steps to run, preview of prompt(s), link to repo + runbook
CLI flow: `rwd proto init chat-with-history` -> clone -> `.env.sample` -> `rwd proto run` -> local http://localhost:3000 with 1-click 'call demo' button
Quick 'share' snippet generation: 'share this prototype' produces a short link + ephemeral demo token for customer calls
